newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHENS BOURSE UNLIKELY TO OPEN ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ATHENS BOURSE UNLIKELY TO OPEN ON TUESDAY.

text.p: The Athens bourse was unlikely to open on Tuesday for a third consecutive working day after national economy ministry officials and stockbroker association representatives failed to resolve a settlement row, brokers said.
Economy ministry officials and the representatives of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA) were due to resume efforts to resolve the crisis on Tuesday morning.

"Right now it looks very unlikely that the exchange will be open tomorrow. The differences between the two sides are just too great," said the head of one large brokerage firm who asked for anonymity.
SMEHA, which groups all 65 Athens securities brokerages, has submitted a list of requests to the bourse governing board and the ministry, including a guarantee of settlement payments.
SMEHA members erupted in anger last week after the bourse's clearing house failed to settle with several members because one firm, Delta Securities, defaulted on its payments.
Delta has been charged with fraud after failing to make a 2.6 billion drachma payment and three top Delta officials have been barred from leaving the country.
SMEHA has asked the national economy ministry to approve a deal to nullify trades between Delta and 11 brokerages from October 30, when Delta paid its settlements with bad cheques.
But brokers said national economy ministry officials told them during a late night meeting on Monday that there were legal problems with all their requests.
Ministry officials said they were trying to find a solution but it was difficult.

"The effort is on the right track. We are hopeful that the exchange will open tomorrow but nothing is sure. We have had endless discussions but the process is continuing," Apostolos Fotiadis, general secretary of the national economy ministry, told Reuters.
"We are set to meet the brokers delegation on Tuesday," he added.

Ministry officials told brokers that 1.35 billion drachmas out of Delta's 2.6 billion drachma default could be covered by the clearing house itself. The remainder would have to be covered by the 11 member firms that were counter-parties to trades with Delta, brokers said.
But past midnight approval for all five items making up the brokers proposal was still pending and there seemed to be wide consensus that the bourse would stay closed on Tuesday.

Athens brokers association (SMEHA) president Panagiotis Kondalexis had returned to the associations members after his meeting at the national economy ministry to discuss the problem. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
